quote_mismatches.quote: Our models showed that the hot subdwarf + white dwarf channel can plausibly explain the properties of D6-2.
The recent discovery of hypervelocity white dwarfs by Shen et al. (2018) provides potential observational evidence for surviving companions of Type Ia supernova explosions.
One of these candidates (D6-2) even traces back to a faint supernova remnant, reinforcing the ejection hypothesis.
Our models showed that the hot subdwarf + white dwarf channel can plausibly explain the properties of D6-2.

The hypervelocity He-rich star US 708 (Hirsch et al. 2005) has been explained as the runaway donor star from a thermonuclear explosion (Justham et al. 2009; Geier et al. 2015; Brown et al. 2015; Neunteufel et al. 2022).

The hypervelocity He-rich star US 708 (Hirsch et al. 2005) has been explained as the runaway donor star from a thermonuclear explosion (Justham et al. 2009; Geier et al. 2015; Brown et al. 2015; Neunteufel et al. 2022).

The orbital velocities of donor stars in this progenitor channel naturally yield orbital velocities consistent with US 708, LP 40–365 stars, and D6-2, indicating that a single class of thermonuclear supernova progenitors can account for their entire range of ejection velocities.
Our models also predict a good fraction of runaway stars with high core He fractions, up to 0.8, which could potentially account for objects like US 708.
